description: Load a customer list in one call — a mailing list, a migration from another system. For one person use create_customer. This is the ONE import that recognises records it already has: pass `rows` and the server looks each one up BY EMAIL, updating that customer instead of duplicating them. A row with no email is always created new and can never be matched again, so push for emails before importing. Fields you pass overwrite the stored ones; fields you omit are left alone — but an address you pass replaces the stored address whole, and `tags` replaces the whole tag list. ALL-OR-NOTHING: unlike the other imports this one runs in a single transaction, so one bad row rolls the entire batch back and nothing is written. There is no per-row failure list. Max 500 rows per call. BEFORE CALLING: show the merchant a preview of the first few rows, state the EXACT number of rows and which resource they hit, and get an explicit yes. There is NO undo and no dry-run — nothing here validates without writing. If you are unsure a row is right, ask; a wrong bulk import is far more expensive to repair than a question. Afterwards, tell the merchant what landed: an import done here does NOT appear in the cabinet's Recent Imports list, which only records uploads made through the wizard.

rows.description: Spreadsheet rows — matched by email, then created or updated by the server

email.description: Strongly recommended — the only key that prevents duplicates

externalId.description: Id in the system the data came from

updates.description: Use only when you already hold the id and do not want email matching

customerId.description: Existing customer id from export_records or get_customers
